pr.title: Show retrying deliveries on the endpoint page
pr.author: example-dev
pr.head: endpoint-retrying

overview.background: Each endpoint, a customer's URL that gets our webhooks, has a page of its own. The page counts the endpoint's deliveries by status. A delivery is one event on its way to that endpoint. #42, the pull request under this one, added a fourth status, retrying: the post failed, and the delivery waits for its next post.
overview.summary: The endpoint page still counted only pending, delivered and failed deliveries. So a delivery that waited for a retry showed nowhere. This pull request counts all four statuses, and shows when the next retry is due.
steps: A new function counts the deliveries in each status and finds the next retry.
The docs describe the counts on the endpoint page.

terms.means: The status of a delivery whose post failed and that waits for its next post, due at `nextAttemptAt`.
The new function that gives the endpoint page its numbers.
When the soonest retrying delivery is due, or `null` when none is retrying.
The interface the code uses to read and write the database.

chapters.title: Counts for every delivery state
body: The endpoint page needs one number per status. The new [`deliveryCounts`](ref:src/api/endpoint.ts:15) gives them: it asks the database for each count, in parallel. It also reads the retrying delivery with the smallest `nextAttemptAt`. That time is `nextRetryAt`, when the next post is due.
`Db` gets `count`, which takes the same filter as `find`. When no delivery is retrying, `nextRetryAt` is `null`.

cells: its own count, with the next post's time

  S --> R["pending, retrying, delivered, failed"]
  F --> N["nextRetryAt, or null with none"]:::new

chapters.title: The endpoint page in the docs
chapters.body: The webhooks guide in `docs/webhooks.md` is for the customers who receive our webhooks. A new section says what the endpoint page counts. It also says that the Retrying count shows when the next post is due.

chapters.title: Tests for the counts
chapters.body: The tests run `deliveryCounts` against a fake database. One test counts a mix of statuses and checks that the soonest retry wins. Another checks that `nextRetryAt` is `null` when no delivery is retrying.

flowchart LR

  T --> B["nothing retrying: nextRetryAt is null"]:::new
